clue.text: Good apartments for chaps getting married

parts.note: apartments are sets of rooms, so rooms stands in for them

explanation.surface: Smart flats are on offer for men about to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Men on their wedding day are bridegrooms, shortened in everyday use to this word.

clue.text: Farmhouse finally looming over mountains

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word looming

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A farmhouse looms at last above the hills behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the second, so G comes before RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings attached, a farmhouse in the old sense.

clue.text: A supporter of motorway development? It takes some swallowing finally

definitions.meaning: read literally, someone in favour of building highways, a person backing tarmac
a last drink downed before leaving a pub or party

explanation.surface: A road-building campaigner, perhaps, and something hard to accept at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes some swallowing' looks like an idiom for something hard to believe, but it is literally a drink to be gulped.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a farewell drink, and read literally it names a backer of highways.

clue.text: After start of match one fellow gets position on cricket field

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the word match

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Once the match begins, a man takes up his fielding spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A university fellow is a don. MID-ON is a fielding position in cricket, close to the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-on is a named fielding place in cricket, on the leg side near the bowler.

clue.text: Looked fixedly about, happy to be outside

indicators.note: the word for happy wraps around the short word for about, so it is outside it

parts.note: glad means happy
re is Latin-derived for about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone stared all around, glad to be out in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare angrily and fixedly, so the past tense matches looked fixedly.

clue.text: The French worker thus put up sheds

parts.note: le is French for the
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word for thus is written upward, so read backwards

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A French labourer erected some sheds in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean-tos are simple sheds built against a wall with a sloping roof, so they are a kind of outbuilding.

clue.text: I meet ignorant rowdy — strict discipline needed

indicators.note: rowdy suggests disorderly behaviour, so the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Faced with a loud, ill-mannered lout, firm control is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimentation means imposing rigid order and uniformity, as in an army regiment.

clue.text: Giving medicine to Carol after party

indicators.note: after places the singing word behind the word for party

parts.note: a do is a party
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone is treated with medicine for over-indulging after a festive party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dose someone is to give them medicine, so the participle fits giving medicine to.

clue.text: Ensure bandage is tight for cow

indicators.note: tight here means drunk, so the letters of these words are reeling about

explanation.surface: Make sure the dressing on the cow is firmly bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' seems to describe the bandage but is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of black beef cattle, so one is a cow.

clue.text: Soldiers inside got rid of — got rid of as evil devils

definitions.text: got rid of as evil devils

indicators.note: inside puts the soldiers within the word for got rid of

parts.note: excised means cut out or removed
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops took out some fiendish demons in a purge.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to drive out evil spirits by ritual, so it means expelling devils.

clue.text: Grumble's increased audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the word for increased is to be heard, not read

parts.note: grown means increased

explanation.surface: Someone's complaining has got louder.
explanation.definitionFit: To groan is to complain or moan, a synonym for grumble.

clue.text: Old Turk's seat

definitions.meaning: a subject of the old Turkish empire founded by Osman
a low upholstered stool or couch without a back

explanation.surface: A seat belonging to an elderly Turkish man.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a member of the historic Turkish empire and a padded backless seat.

clue.text: Putting slant on things, the way a printer does?

definitions.text: Putting slant on things, the way a printer does?

parts.words: Putting slant on things, the way a printer does?
parts.note: putting a slant on things suggests spin or bias, but a printer slants type into sloping letters

explanation.surface: Someone is giving events a biased spin, much as a printer might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting slant on things' suggests twisting the facts; the printer turns it into sloping type.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so setting text that way puts a literal slant on it.

clue.text: Presented unruly fellow, having brought in help

indicators.note: the fellow takes the help inside himself, enclosing it

parts.note: a lout is a boorish, unruly man
aid means help

explanation.surface: A troublemaker was introduced once he had called for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means arranged and set out for display, so it can mean presented.

clue.text: Former PM's wastelands?

parts.note: Edward Heath was a UK Conservative prime minister of 1970-74
the possessive ending supplies its S as written

explanation.surface: Does some open ground belong to an ex-prime minister?
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was British prime minister 1970-74; his name plus the possessive S gives the plural word.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaths are open, uncultivated tracts of scrubby land, a kind of wasteland.

clue.text: Surly Conservative out of touch?

parts.note: rusty means out of practice, out of touch with a skill

explanation.surface: A grumpy Tory who has lost touch with ordinary life.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusty describes someone irritable and curt in manner, much like surly.

clue.text: See mine blowing up fighters on the other side

indicators.note: a mine blowing up scatters things, so these letters are blasted into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch a landmine explode among the opposing troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy are the opposing forces in a war, so its plural means hostile fighters.

clue.text: Companion has manner that goes with professorial position

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: An associate has the bearing that suits a university professor.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called a chair, as in holding the chair of history.

clue.text: Idiot given hard material

parts.note: clot is British slang for a fool
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fool is handed some tough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth is woven fabric, the everyday sense of material.

clue.text: Something that has to be seen will be spoiling daughter?

definitions.text: Something that has to be seen
definitions.meaning: a must-see event or show, an opportunity not to pass up
read whimsically: being excessively kind to a young unmarried girl, a Miss

explanation.surface: A show not to be missed, and a parent who spoils a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: indulging a daughter means being over-kind to Miss, the title of a young unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an event or chance so attractive one must not pass it up.

clue.text: Solemn — is teased terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of teased are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grave person has been mocked dreadfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, dignified and serious, close to solemn.

clue.text: Quiet sweetheart may be a hypocrite

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
honey is a term of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken lover might turn out to be two-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun a phoney is a fraud or pretender, someone insincere like a hypocrite.
